payload.description: The open-source app everyone uses to manage agents at work

payload.text:
Quickstart · Docs · GitHub · Discord · Twitter · Website



# Paperclip is the app people use to manage AI agents for work. Open-source orchestration for teams of AI agents. **If OpenClaw is an _employee_, Paperclip is the _company_.** Paperclip is a Node.js server and React UI that orchestrates a team of AI agents to run a business. Bring your own agents, assign goals, and track work and costs from one dashboard. It looks like a task manager. Under the hood: org charts, budgets, governance, goal alignment, and agent coordination. **Manage business goals, not pull requests.** | | Step | Example | | ------ | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **01** | Define the goal | _"Build the #1 AI note-taking app to $1M MRR."_ | | **02** | Hire the team | CEO, CTO, engineers, designers, marketers — any bot, any provider. | | **03** | Approve and run | Review strategy. Set budgets. Hit go. Monitor from the dashboard. |
Works
with
OpenClaw
Claude Code
Codex
Cursor
Bash
HTTP
If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired.

## Paperclip is right for you if - ✅ You want to build **autonomous AI companies** - ✅ You **coordinate many different agents** (OpenClaw, Codex, Claude, Cursor) toward a common goal - ✅ You have **20 simultaneous Claude Code terminals** open and lose track of what everyone is doing - ✅ You want agents running **autonomously 24/7**, but still want to audit work and chime in when needed - ✅ You want to **monitor costs** and enforce budgets - ✅ You want a process for managing agents that **feels like using a task manager** - ✅ You want to manage your autonomous businesses **from your phone**
## Features

🔌 Bring Your Own Agent

Any agent, any runtime, one org chart. If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired.

🎯 Goal Alignment

Every task traces back to the company mission. Agents know what to do and why.

💓 Heartbeats

Agents wake on a schedule, check work, and act. Delegation flows up and down the org chart.

💰 Cost Control

Monthly budgets per agent. When they hit the limit, they stop. No runaway costs.

🏢 Multi-Company

One deployment, many companies. Complete data isolation. One control plane for your portfolio.

🎫 Ticket System

Every conversation traced. Every decision explained. Full tool-call tracing and immutable audit log.

🛡️ Governance

Approve hires, override strategy, pause or terminate any agent — at any time.

📊 Org Chart

Hierarchies, roles, reporting lines. Your agents have a boss, a title, and a job description.

📱 Mobile Ready

Monitor and manage your autonomous businesses from anywhere.

## Problems Paperclip solves | Without Paperclip | With Paperclip | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | ❌ You have 20 Claude Code tabs open and can't track which one does what. On reboot you lose everything. | ✅ Tasks are ticket-based, conversations are threaded, sessions persist across reboots. | | ❌ You manually gather context from several places to remind your bot what you're actually doing. | ✅ Context flows from the task up through the project and company goals — your agent always knows what to do and why. | | ❌ Folders of agent configs are disorganized and you're re-inventing task management, communication, and coordination between agents. | ✅ Paperclip gives you org charts, ticketing, delegation, and governance out of the box — so you run a company, not a pile of scripts. | | ❌ Runaway loops waste hundreds of dollars of tokens and max your quota before you even know what happened. | ✅ Cost tracking surfaces token budgets and throttles agents when they're out. Management prioritizes with budgets. | | ❌ You have recurring jobs (customer support, social, reports) and have to remember to manually kick them off. | ✅ Heartbeats handle regular work on a schedule. Management supervises. | | ❌ You have an idea, you have to find your repo, fire up Claude Code, keep a tab open, and babysit it. | ✅ Add a task in Paperclip. Your coding agent works on it until it's done. Management reviews their work. |
## Why Paperclip is special Paperclip handles the hard orchestration details correctly. | | | | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Atomic execution.** | Task checkout and budget enforcement are atomic, so no double-work and no runaway spend. | | **Persistent agent state.** | Agents resume the same task context across heartbeats instead of restarting from scratch. | | **Runtime skill injection.** | Agents can learn Paperclip workflows and project context at runtime, without retraining. | | **Governance with rollback.** | Approval gates are enforced, config changes are revisioned, and bad changes can be rolled back safely. | | **Goal-aware execution.** | Tasks carry full goal ancestry so agents consistently see the "why," not just a title. | | **Portable company templates.** | Export/import orgs, agents, and skills with secret scrubbing and collision handling. | | **True multi-company isolation.** | Every entity is company-scoped, so one deployment can run many companies with separate data and audit trails. |
## What's Under the Hood Paperclip is a full control plane, not a wrapper. Before you build any of this yourself, know that it already exists: ``` ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ PAPERCLIP SERVER │ │ │ │ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ │ │ │Identity & │ │ Work & │ │ Heartbeat │ │Governance │ │ │ │ Access │ │ Tasks │ │ Execution │ │& Approvals│ │ │ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ │ │ │ Org Chart │ │Workspaces │ │ Plugins │ │ Budget │ │ │ │ & Agents │ │ & Runtime │ │ │ │ & Costs │ │ │ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ │ │ │ Routines │ │ Secrets & │ │ Activity │ │ Company │ │ │ │& Schedules│ │ Storage │ │ & Events │ │Portability│ │ │ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ▲ ▲ ▲ ▲ ┌─────┴─────┐ ┌─────┴─────┐ ┌─────┴─────┐ ┌─────┴─────┐ │ Claude │ │ Codex │ │ CLI │ │ HTTP/web │ │ Code │ │ │ │ agents │ │ bots │ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ ``` ### The Systems
**Identity & Access** — Two deployment modes (trusted local or authenticated), board users, agent API keys, short-lived run JWTs, company memberships, invite flows, and OpenClaw onboarding. Every mutating request is traced to an actor. **Org Chart & Agents** — Agents have roles, titles, reporting lines, permissions, and budgets. Adapter examples match the diagram: Claude Code, Codex, CLI agents such as Cursor/Gemini/bash, HTTP/webhook bots such as OpenClaw, and external adapter plugins. If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired.
**Work & Task System** — Issues carry company/project/goal/parent links, atomic checkout with execution locks, first-class blocker dependencies, comments, documents, attachments, work products, labels, and inbox state. No double-work, no lost context. **Heartbeat Execution** — DB-backed wakeup queue with coalescing, budget checks, workspace resolution, secret injection, skill loading, and adapter invocation. Runs produce structured logs, cost events, session state, and audit trails. Recovery handles orphaned runs automatically.
**Workspaces & Runtime** — Project workspaces, isolated execution workspaces (git worktrees, operator branches), and runtime services (dev servers, preview URLs). Agents work in the right directory with the right context every time. **Governance & Approvals** — Board approval workflows, execution policies with review/approval stages, decision tracking, budget hard-stops,

# Contributing Guide

Thanks for wanting to contribute!

We really appreciate both small fixes and thoughtful larger changes.

## Two Paths to Get Your Pull Request Accepted

### Path 1: Small, Focused Changes (Fastest way to get merged)

- Pick **one** clear thing to fix/improve
- Touch the **smallest possible number of files**
- Make sure the change is very targeted and easy to review
- All tests pass and CI is green
- Greptile score is 5/5 with all comments addressed
- Use the [PR template](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md)

These almost always get merged quickly when they're clean.

### Path 2: Bigger or Impactful Changes

- **First** talk about it in Discord → #dev channel  
  → Describe what you're trying to solve  
  → Share rough ideas / approach
- Once there's rough agreement, build it
- In your PR include:
  - Before / After screenshots (or short video if UI/behavior change)
  - Clear description of what & why
  - Proof it works (manual testing notes)
  - All tests passing and CI green
  - Greptile score 5/5 with all comments addressed
  - [PR template](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md) fully filled out

PRs that follow this path are **much** more likely to be accepted, even when they're large.

## PR Requirements (all PRs)

### Use the PR Template

Every pull request **must** follow the PR template at [`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md). If you create a PR via the GitHub API or other tooling that bypasses the template, copy its contents into your PR description manually. The template includes required sections: Thinking Path, What Changed, Verification, Risks, Model Used, and a Checklist.

### Model Used (Required)

Every PR must include a **Model Used** section specifying which AI model produced or assisted with the change. Include the provider, exact model ID/version, context window size, and any relevant capability details (e.g., reasoning mode, tool use). If no AI was used, write "None — human-authored". This applies to all contributors — human and AI alike.

### Tests Must Pass

All tests must pass before a PR can be merged. Run them locally first and verify CI is green after pushing.

### Greptile Review

We use [Greptile](https://greptile.com) for automated code review. Your PR must achieve a **5/5 Greptile score** with **all Greptile comments addressed** before it can be merged. If Greptile leaves comments, fix or respond to each one and request a re-review.

## Feature Contributions

We actively manage the core Paperclip feature roadmap.

Uncoordinated feature PRs against the core product may be closed, even when the implementation is thoughtful and high quality. That is about roadmap ownership, product coherence, and long-term maintenance commitment, not a judgment about the effort.

If you want to contribute a feature:

- Check [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) first
- Start the discussion in Discord -> `#dev` before writing code
- If the idea fits as an extension, prefer building it with the [plugin system](doc/plugins/PLUGIN_SPEC.md)
- If you want to show a possible direction, reference implementations are welcome as feedback, but they generally will not be merged directly into core

Bugs, docs improvements, and small targeted improvements are still the easiest path to getting merged, and we really do appreciate them.

## General Rules (both paths)

- Write clear commit messages
- Keep PR title + description meaningful
- One PR = one logical change (unless it's a small related group)
- Run tests locally first
- Be kind in discussions 😄

## Writing a Good PR message

Your PR description must follow the [PR template](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md). All sections are required. The "thinking path" at the top explains from the top of the project down to what you fixed. E.g.:

### Thinking Path Example 1:

> - Paperclip orchestrates ai-agents for zero-human companies
> - There are many types of adapters for each LLM model provider
> - But LLM's have a context limit and not all agents can automatically compact their context
> - So we need to have an adapter-specific configuration for which adapters can and cannot automatically compact their context
> - This pull request adds per-adapter configuration of compaction, either auto or paperclip managed
> - That way we can get optimal performance from any adapter/provider in Paperclip

### Thinking Path Example 2:

> - Paperclip orchestrates ai-agents for zero-human companies
> - But humans want to watch the agents and oversee their work
> - Human users also operate in teams and so they need their own logins, profiles, views etc.
> - So we have a multi-user system for humans
> - But humans want to be able to update their own profile picture and avatar
> - But the avatar upload form wasn't saving the avatar to the file storage system
> - So this PR fixes the avatar upload form to use the file storage service
> - The benefit is we don't have a one-off file storage for just one aspect of the system, which would cause confusion and extra configuration

Then have the rest of your normal PR message after the Thinking Path.

This should include details about what you did, why you did it, why it matters & the benefits, how we can verify it works, and any risks.

Please include screenshots if possible if you have a visible change. (use something like the [agent-browser skill](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser/blob/main/skills/agent-browser/SKILL.md) or similar to take screenshots). Ideally, you include before and after screenshots.

Questions? Just ask in #dev — we're happy to help.

Happy hacking!

payload.title: Add documents array to issue payload

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds a `documents` field to the return value of `getIssueDocumentPayload` in `server/src/services/documents.ts`, exposing full document bodies inline on the issue payload (mirroring the existing `GET /issues/:id/documents` endpoint). - The new `documents` field maps the same filtered `documentSummaries` rows with `includeBody=true`, so full document bodies now appear in issue GET/list responses without an extra round-trip. - `filterSystemDocuments` is called twice with identical arguments (once for `documentSummaries`, once for `documents`); a shared intermediate variable would be cleaner. - The response will now include all document data twice — once without body (`documentSummaries`) and once with body (`documents`) — which may noticeably increase payload size for issues with many or large documents.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The change is additive and backward-compatible; the main consideration is increased response payload size for issues with many or large documents. The change introduces one small redundancy — the same filter is applied twice to the same array — but the logic is otherwise correct and isolated to a single return object. The bigger practical concern is that every issue GET response will now carry all document bodies inline, which could noticeably increase payload size at scale. Neither issue is blocking, but the payload growth is worth conscious review before merging. server/src/services/documents.ts — specifically the double filterSystemDocuments call and the cumulative payload size implications for issues with many large documents.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | server/src/services/documents.ts | Adds `documents` field (with full bodies) to `getIssueDocumentPayload` return object; `filterSystemDocuments` is called twice on the same array where one filtered result variable would suffice. |

Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 server/src/services/documents.ts:135-139 `filterSystemDocuments` is called twice with identical arguments — once for `documentSummaries` and again for `documents`. Since it is a pure filter over the same array, extracting it to a local variable avoids redundant iteration. ```suggestion planDocument: planDocument ? mapIssueDocumentRow(planDocument, true) : null, ...((() => { const filtered = filterSystemDocuments(documentSummaries, options.includeSystem ?? false); return { documentSummaries: filtered.map((row) => mapIssueDocumentRow(row, false)), documents: filtered.map((row) => mapIssueDocumentRow(row, true)), }; })()), ``` `````

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds a first-class `executionLabelIds` field to routines so that labels can be pre-assigned to every execution issue without relying on fragile text instructions in the routine description. The change spans the full stack: DB migration, Drizzle schema, shared types/validators, server routes, service logic, portability export/import, and plugin-managed routines. - **Migration & schema** — `IF NOT EXISTS` guard makes the column safe to add repeatedly; Drizzle schema and default align correctly. - **Service layer** — Label IDs are validated against the company at create/update time and passed through to `issueSvc.create()` at dispatch; the dual-name (`labelIds`/`executionLabelIds`) resolution is handled consistently. - **Two issues need resolution before merge**: (1) the `labelIds: string[]` field is required on the shared `Routine` interface but is only populated by the routes layer; (2) the portability import passes source-company label IDs directly to `routines.create()`, throwing 422 for cross-company imports instead of gracefully defaulting to `[]`.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge once the cross-company portability import path is hardened and the `labelIds` type/factory gap is resolved. The core create/update/dispatch path is solid, but two gaps remain: the portability import will throw 422 instead of silently resetting to `[]` when label IDs from the source company don't exist in the target, which breaks cross-company data migration; and `labelIds: string[]` is declared required on the shared `Routine` interface while the service layer never populates it, leaving test factories and any internal consumers structurally incomplete. `server/src/services/company-portability.ts` (import throws instead of defaulting to `[]`) and `packages/shared/src/types/routine.ts` (required `labelIds` field not populated by service layer).

Important Files Changed

[]` via spread; the null-return path for update is handled correctly. | | server/src/services/routines.ts | Label ID validation against company scope is correctly added for both create and update paths; execution dispatch passes `executionLabelIds` to issue creation. | | server/src/services/company-portability.ts | Export now serializes `executionLabelIds`; import passes the exported IDs to `routines.create()` without cross-company filtering, throwing 422 for any cross-company import where the source had non-empty label IDs. |

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
Greptile Summary

This PR bundles the `wireframe` skill into the `@paperclipai/skills-catalog` package under `catalog/bundled/product/wireframe`, making it discoverable and installable by any Paperclip agent. It also regenerates the catalog manifest (8 → 9 skills) and refines the shipped-catalog test invariant to block only `scripts_executables` trust level instead of requiring `markdown_only`, aligning the test with the server's actual install-time gate (`assertCatalogSkillInstallable`). - **New skill**: `SKILL.md` + three `references/` docs + two SVG canvas templates + one HTML review-viewer template, all with `trustLevel: assets`. - **Catalog manifest**: regenerated deterministically; wireframe entry is internally consistent (`id`/`key`/`kind`/`category`/`slug`, file inventory, `contentHash`). - **Test update**: invariant correctly relaxed to `scripts_executables` boundary; expected key set updated with the new bundled key.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; the change is purely additive catalog content and a test-invariant relaxation that matches the server's existing install-time gate. All catalog metadata is self-consistent, the manifest is deterministically regenerated, and the test change correctly mirrors the server's assertCatalogSkillInstallable logic. The only findings are accessibility gaps in the site-template.html lightbox (static aria-hidden attribute never toggled, close control not keyboard-reachable), which will propagate to every agent-generated review page but do not affect catalog integrity or install correctness. packages/skills-catalog/catalog/bundled/product/wireframe/assets/site-template.html — lightbox accessibility fixes before copying this template becomes widespread

Greptile Summary

This PR implements two defense-in-depth security controls: R4 fully redacts `adapterConfig` and `runtimeConfig` env bindings (including vault UUIDs) in board-facing GET responses, and R5 adds a strict Zod schema that returns 400 with per-key path errors when a sensitive env key (matched by `SENSITIVE_ENV_KEY_VALIDATOR_RE`) is submitted with a `{type:\"plain\"}` binding. - **R4 (redaction):** `redactAdapterConfig` in `server/src/redaction.ts` unconditionally redacts every env binding value regardless of key name; `buildAgentDetail` in `agents.ts` now applies this to both `adapterConfig` and `runtimeConfig` for non-restricted views. - **R5 (validator):** `strictEnvConfigSchema` in `secret.ts` replaces `envConfigSchema` in `adapterConfigSchema`; the regex covers 14+ key classes and per-key Zod issues are propagated with full path context. - **Gap:** The strict validator probes only `envBindingPlainSchema` (the `{type:\"plain\"}` object form) and skips raw string bindings — `envBindingSchema` also accepts bare strings as a legacy form, so `{GITHUB_TOKEN: \"ghp_...\"}` passes the R5 check without triggering a 400.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The test suite only exercises the type=plain and secret_ref forms and does not catch this case. packages/shared/src/validators/secret.ts — the superRefine logic and its accompanying tests need to cover the raw-string binding case for sensitive keys.

Added a second commit (f74875ca) to this PR covering the OOM side of the same problem:

- Writes `oom_score_adj=500` to `/proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj` immediately after spawning each agent subprocess — makes the kernel prefer killing agent/test processes over the Paperclip server when memory is tight
- Companion change: added `OOMScoreAdjust=-500` to the local `paperclip.service` systemd unit (not in this repo)
- Added `memory=32GB` cap to `.wslconfig` to prevent WSL2 from consuming all host RAM

Root cause of this second commit: a pytest run in a worktree consumed ~35GB RAM, triggering OOM-kill of the Paperclip service and embedded postgres mid-query, causing `the database system is shutting down` errors and UI "failed to fetch".

payload.author: mrveiss
payload.body:
**New commit added to this branch:** `a6c13d9` — fix(heartbeat): 10-min grace period for local runs with no stored PID

This extends the shutdown-kill fix with a complementary startup fix. The problem: on restart, `reapOrphanedRuns()` (called with `staleThresholdMs=0`) finds runs where `processPid=null` (server crashed before `persistRunProcessMetadata` ran), assumes the process died, and immediately re-dispatches — while the original process is still alive as an orphan. Each restart cycle multiplies the orphan count exponentially.

The fix adds a 10-minute grace window for null-PID local-adapter runs so the slot stays occupied and the `maxConcurrentRuns` cap remains enforced. After the grace period the slot is reclaimed normally.

Issue filed: #7270
Tests: 2 new cases added, 46/46 passing.

payload.body:
Greptile Summary

This PR is described as adding bulk `.env` file upload to the env-var editor, but the automated "overnight sprint" agent that produced it has gone severely off-rails, destroying large parts of the codebase alongside the intended feature work. - **The feature itself** (`EnvVarEditor.tsx`, `secrets.ts`, `agents.ts`, `cli/src/commands/client/secrets.ts`) is reasonably implemented: a dotenv parser, an upload button that auto-seals sensitive keys as secrets, a new `strictModeKeys` option for PATCH paths, and `rotate`/`delete` CLI subcommands. - **`server/src/services/issues.ts`** has been truncated from 6,089 lines to 1,786, ending mid-word (`[...new Set(iss`). Every issue-listing, filtering, comment, approval, and dependency function defined after line 1,786 has been deleted. The server will fail to compile. - **`server/src/services/execution-workspaces.ts`** has been truncated from 792 lines to 37 — a raw method fragment with no imports, no module wrapper, and no exports. Five other files that should not exist in the repo have also been committed: `pf_wrapper.py` (a developer-local CTO agent wrapper containing SQL-injection vulnerabilities), `mini_runner.py`, `mini_textbased.yaml`, `server/src/routes/issues.ts.rej`, and `server/src/services/issues.ts.patch`. A git submodule (`paperclip`) has been added at the repo root unintentionally. The PR description also does not meet the requirements in CONTRIBUTING.md (no thinking path, no verification steps, no risks section, no Model Used section), and the UI change has no accompanying screenshots.

Confidence Score: 1/5

Do not merge — two core server modules are fatally truncated, a git submodule and personal-machine infrastructure scripts have been added unintentionally, and merge artifacts are committed to the repo. The issues service (6,089 → 1,786 lines, ending mid-word) and execution-workspaces service (792 → 37 lines, unparseable fragment) are both destroyed. The server cannot compile in this state. On top of that, pf_wrapper.py ships two SQL injection paths against the application database, and several files that have no place in a shared repository have been committed. The actual dotenv-upload feature in EnvVarEditor.tsx, secrets.ts, and agents.ts looks correct in isolation, but it is buried inside a change set that would take the entire application offline. server/src/services/issues.ts and server/src/services/execution-workspaces.ts must be restored from the base branch. pf_wrapper.py, mini_runner.py, mini_textbased.yaml, server/src/routes/issues.ts.rej, server/src/services/issues.ts.patch, and the paperclip submodule must all be removed before the feature changes can be evaluated on their own merits.

Security Review

 - **SQL injection — `pf_wrapper.py` `_get_company_id` (line ~197):** `issue_id` from the `PAPERCLIP_TASK_ID` environment variable is concatenated directly into a `psql` query string with no escaping or parameterisation. - **SQL injection — `pf_wrapper.py` `_post_comment` (lines ~212–226):** `company_id` and `issue_id` are concatenated into an `INSERT` statement. The `body` field uses `$PFBODY$` dollar-quoting, but if agent stdout contains the literal string `$PFBODY$`, the quoting terminates early and the remainder of the body becomes unescaped SQL.

Important Files Changed
